scenarios.title: Coupon Stacking via Concurrent HTTP Request Race Condition
abuseSequence: Attacker initializes a cart with $150 of merchandise across session ID sess_abc123.
Attacker prepares 10 concurrent HTTP POST requests to /api/cart/apply-coupon with identical payload and cookie headers.
Attacker fires all 10 requests simultaneously within a 5ms window via HTTP/2 multiplexed single-packet connection.
The backend worker threads concurrently read the coupon state before any thread commits the 'is_redeemed=true' record in PostgreSQL.
The coupon credit is deducted 6 times against the cart balance, reducing total cart cost to $0 while issuing negative line items.
scenarios.businessImpact: Severe financial leakage through unauthorized product acquisition and coupon budget exhaustion.
detectionSignals: Multiple POST /api/cart/apply-coupon requests from identical session within 50ms window
Cart checkout total computed as zero or negative despite positive retail item values
Audit log anomaly: coupon_redemptions table records multiple entries for single-use coupon ID
mitigations: Implement strict row-level database locking ('SELECT ... FOR UPDATE') on coupon state records during transaction validation
Enforce distributed Redis mutex locks or atomic SETNX keys keyed on `coupon:${couponId}:${userId}` with a 15-second TTL
Enforce an explicit check constraint in the database preventing cart totals less than minimum allowed order value
scenarios.pentestTestCase:
```bash

    for i in range(15):
        engine.queue(req, gate='race1')
    engine.openGate('race1')
```

scenarios.title: Payment Settlement Step Bypass via Direct State Machine Jump
preconditions: Active shopping cart draft initialized at step 1
abuseSequence: Attacker creates an order draft via POST /api/orders/create and receives order ID 'ord_778129' in state 'PENDING_PAYMENT'.
Instead of posting payment token to /api/orders/ord_778129/pay, attacker directly issues POST to /api/orders/ord_778129/confirm.
The confirmation endpoint fails to check if 'payment_status == PAID' and transitions the order state directly to 'CONFIRMED' and queues warehouse dispatch.
scenarios.businessImpact: Immediate inventory theft and unfulfilled revenue collection due to shipping un-paid orders.
detectionSignals: Order state change event to 'CONFIRMED' without preceding 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED' webhook or ledger log
Zero payment gateway authorization ID or transaction reference attached to confirmed order record
mitigations: Enforce strict Finite State Machine (FSM) validation: transition to 'CONFIRMED' is rejected by state machine unless state is 'PAYMENT_VERIFIED'
Require cryptographically signed state transition tokens or server-side session assertions before invoking the fulfillment pipeline

scenarios.title: Self-Approval and Tenant Organization IDOR in Payment Batch Release
preconditions: Standard invoice creator role in Tenant Org A
abuseSequence: Attacker uploads invoice draft #9021 via POST /api/invoices.
Attacker submits invoice to approval queue via POST /api/invoices/9021/submit.
Attacker intercepts the approval request and substitutes their own session token while calling PATCH /api/invoices/9021/approve, modifying 'approverOrgId' to match Tenant Org B.
The authorization handler checks role presence ('is_manager') without scoping validation to whether the manager belongs to the organization owning invoice #9021.
scenarios.businessImpact: Unauthorized fund disbursement, cross-tenant compliance breach, and fraudulent vendor payouts.
detectionSignals: Approver user ID and creator user ID belong to conflicting tenant organizations in invoice audit log
Disbursement approvals originating from IP addresses unassociated with the designated finance manager
mitigations: Enforce tenant-scoped database queries with composite keys `WHERE id = ? AND org_id = ?`
Implement mandatory separation of duties (SoD) rule preventing the creator user ID from matching the approver user ID regardless of role
